title: Radial Arm Water Maze Protocol
author: Mari Golub
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.yv2fw8e
materials: Do not remove animal from water when re-placing.

steps.title: Prepare Experimental Design and Scheduling
steps.instruction: Establish the testing schedule and group assignments to minimize bias and performance variance.

substeps.instruction: Schedule testing during the same 2-3 hour period each day (morning or afternoon, at least one hour prior to dark cycle onset).
Ensure each 9-day trial begins on the same day of the week for all cohorts.
Separate males and females into different test groups (8 or 16 animals per group), preferably in different cohorts and after a water change.
Randomize the test order of experimental groups across all cohorts.
Maintain blinding by omitting experimental group designations from animal housing, lab schedules, and data sheets until study completion.
Standardize caging and record cage designations in the dataset to identify cagemates.
If 4-5 mice of the same group are housed together, separate them into individual cages prior to each day of testing and recombine them after testing.

steps.title: Set Up RAWM Apparatus
steps.instruction: Assemble and calibrate the six-arm apparatus (30.5" diameter, 8" high, 10" long, 5 5/8" wide) in a swim pool to create an 11" diameter middle free area.

substeps.instruction: Place the apparatus on a table in maze room (MBP Rm112) and level it by adjusting the table legs.
Add Tempura paint to the water until the platform is not visible; stir the water prior to testing each day to ensure even opacity.
Adjust water temperature to 21 degrees centigrade.
Set up room lighting using side lights only (no overhead room lights).
Ensure room cues are present: furniture, poster, ceiling mounted cameras, 10-inch diameter circular wall clock, 8 x 10 inch paper towel dispenser, and the investigator.
Place the 2.5" round escape platform 1.0 cm below the water surface at the end of the designated arm, with the base touching the end of the arm.

steps.title: Perform Daily Testing Sessions
steps.instruction: Conduct 9 daily sessions consisting of 5 trials each per animal.

substeps.instruction: Place animal home cages on a heating pad in the testing room.
Remove the animal from the home cage by the tail (do not place in palm).
Release the animal in the apparatus facing the middle at the end of the start arm.
Position the investigator between arms 3 and 4 at the tub to place the mouse without moving; position the scorer by the tabletop by arm 2.
Observe the animal for 60 seconds or until it finds the platform; do not remove the animal from water when re-placing.
Record if the animal circles or floats (Y/N).
Count and record the number of errors and the latency to reach the platform.
Allow the animal 30s of platform familiarization at the conclusion of the trial; if the animal did not find the platform, guide it across the water to the platform.
For trials 1-4: Start the next trial immediately after the 30s platform period (no drying off).
For trial 5 (retention trial): Wait 30-40 minutes after the end of the fourth trial. During this interval, dry the animal and place it in the warmed home cage.

steps.title: Maintain Apparatus Hygiene
steps.instruction: Clean and disinfect the maze on specific days to maintain experimental integrity.

substeps.instruction: On day 5: Drain and rinse the maze and tub with clean water, disinfect all surfaces with 10% nolvasan solution, re-rinse with fresh water, and refill with fresh water and paint to correct opacity.
On day 9: Repeat the cleaning process (drain, rinse, disinfect with 10% nolvasan, re-rinse); do not refill with water/paint if no further testing is conducted.

steps.title: Manage and Analyze Data
steps.instruction: Record all trial parameters on log sheets and transcribe them into the study dataset (one row per mouse).

substeps.instruction: Record the following for each trial: test order, total errors, latency (sec), floating behavior (y/n), and circling behavior (y/n).
Log the start time for the first 4 trials, the end time for the 4th trial, and the start time for the 5th trial.
Calculate average latency for all 5 trials per day and the average time from start to platform across all days.

Calculate average errors for: all Trial 4; Days 8 and 9 Trial 4; Days 8 and 9 Trial 5; all Trial 1-4; all Trial 5; (all Trial 5 minus all Trial 4); and (Days 8 and 9 Trial 5 minus Days 8 and 9 Trial 4).
Maintain a log of protocol deviations to evaluate outliers.
Include the radial arm water maze codebook (Excel spreadsheet) in the dataset.
